document.tekst_begin: Beste griffie, Afgelopen week verscheen het nieuws van het faillissement van Bedrocan, de enige Nederlandse teler van medicinale cannabis. Het faillissement hangt samen met de beëindiging van de samenwerking tussen het kabinet en Bedrocan, en laat patiënten in grote onzekerheid achter. Ondertussen is de beantwoording van het schriftelijk overleg Voortgang beleids- en wetswijzigingen medicinale cannabis (d.d. 24 september 2026, 14.00 uur) nog niet binnen. Graag doe ik namens het lid Sneller het verzoek om een kabinetsreactie over het bericht Curator zit met honderden kilo's medicinale wiet na failliet enige Nederlandse teler uiterlijk vrijdag 23 oktober te ontvangen. Artikel 3 Deze wet treedt in werking met ingang van de dag na de datum van uitgifte van het Staatsblad waarin zij wordt geplaatst en werkt terug tot en met 15 september 2026. kst-37035-XXIII-1 ISSN 0921 - 7371 ’s-Gravenhage 202

items.titel: Beslisnota bij verslag houdende een lijst van vragen en antwoorden over vaststelling van de begrotingsstaten van het Ministerie van Binnenlandse Zaken en Koninkrijksrelaties (VII) voor het jaar 2027 (Kamerstuk 37020-VII)
items.samenvatting_bron: None. Zaak:

document.tekst_begin: Aanleiding De Tweede Kamer heeft schriftelijke vragen gesteld over de ontwerpbegroting 2027 Binnenlandse Zaken en Koninkrijksrelaties (VII). Bij dezen leggen wij u de beantwoording voor. Uiterlijk 22 oktober wenst de Kamer de beantwoording te ontvangen. Geadviseerd besluit • Akkoord gaan met de beantwoording op de schriftelijke Kamervragen over de ontwerpbegroting 2027 Binnenlandse Zaken en Koninkrijksrelaties. • MinBZK: De aanbiedingsbrief ondertekenen. Indien u opmerkingen hebt bij de voorliggende beantwoording, zullen wij deze opmerkingen verwerken en de beantwoording opnieuw aan u voorleggen. Kern Er zijn 105 vragen gesteld over de ontwerpbegroting 2027 van BZK. De vragen gaan met name over Herstel Groningen, lokale bestuurders, beleidsdoelen in de begroting, taakstellingen, FIMI-detectie en discriminatie. Ook zijn er enkele vragen over externe inhuur, vergunningsaanvragen, de taskforces, democratie, het gemeenschapsfonds, de budgetflexibiliteit van een aantal begrotingsartikelen en over het slavernijverleden. Toelichting Deze schriftelijke vragen zijn gesteld in de aanloop naar de begrotingsbehandeling van BZK op 3 en 5 november. De Kamer heeft ook schriftelijke vragen gestel

De bepalingen van deze paragraaf zijn van toepassing op bij algemene maatregel van bestuur aangewezen categorieën van ondernemingen. 2. Het voorgestelde artikel 49e wordt als volgt gewijzigd: a. Voor de tekst wordt de aanduiding «2.» geplaatst en in de tekst wordt «Onze Minister zendt» vervangen door «Onverminderd het eerste lid zendt Onze Minister» en wordt «vijf jaar» vervangen door «drie jaar». b. Voor het tweede lid (nieuw) wordt een lid ingevoegd, luidende: 1. Onze Minister zendt een jaar na de inwerkingtreding van deze paragraaf aan de Staten-Generaal een verslag waarin de resultaten van een invoeringstoets over de doeltreffendheid

document.tekst_begin: Tweede Kamer der Staten-Generaal 2 Vergaderjaar 2025–2026 36 835 Implementatie van Richtlijn (EU) 2024/1712 van het Europees Parlement en de Raad van 13 juni 2024 tot wijziging van Richtlijn 2011/36/EU inzake de voorkoming en bestrijding van mensenhandel en de bescherming van slachtoffers daarvan (Implementatiewet herziene Europese richtlijn mensenhandel) Nr. 8 AMENDEMENT VAN HET LID FABER Ontvangen 24 augustus 2026 De ondergetekende stelt het volgende amendement voor: Voor de punt aan het slot van artikel I, onderdeel A, wordt ingevoegd «, en wordt aan dat lid toegevoegd «, alsmede het door een ouder vooruit- sturen van een alleenstaande minderjarige vreemdeling met het oogmerk als ouder van dat kind een verblijfsrecht te verwerven krachtens artikel 29c, eerste lid, onderdeel c, van de Vreemdelingenwet 2000»». Toelichting Indiener wil als extra categorie van uitbuiting toevoegen aan artikel 273f van het Wetboek van Strafrecht het door de ouder(s) vooruitsturen van een minderjarig kind naar Nederland. Het kind wordt misbruikt door de ouders, doordat zij uit eigen gewin het lot van hun eigen minderjarige kind in handen leggen van het circuit van mensensmokkelaars en mensenhandelaars

Dit onderzoek brengt deze casuïstiek voor het eerst op landelijke schaal in beeld en laat zien welke invloed zij heeft op de jeugdzorguitgaven van gemeenten. De resultaten bieden een feitelijke basis voor het vervolg van de discussie over de verdeling van middelen binnen de Jeugdwet. Het onderzoek is beschrijvend van aard en doet geen uitspraken over beleidskeuzes of aanpassingen van de financieringssystematiek. Belangrijkste bevindingen Een beperkte groep jeugdigen legt een steeds groter beslag op de totale jeugdzorguitgaven. Het aantal jeugdigen met jaarlijkse jeugdzorguitgaven boven €100.000 is naar schatting gestegen van circa 5.400 in 2022 naar circa 9.600 in 2024. De bijbehorende uitgaven namen toe van circa €780 miljoen naar circa €1,66 miljard. document.tekst_begin: Bestuurlijke uitgangspunten rondom voorkomen en verkorten van open residentiële jeugdhulp Opgave Jeugdigen zo thuis mogelijk laten opgroeien is een belangrijke opgave binnen de jeugdhulp waar partijen, vanuit hun eigen rol en verantwoordelijkheid, de afgelopen jaren op hebben ingezet. Afhankelijk van de situatie, kan zo thuis mogelijk er op verschillende manieren uitzien. Idealiter groeien jeugdigen in hun eigen thuissituatie op, met ambulante hulp indien nodig. Als dat niet lukt, spelen pleegzorg en gezinshuizen in de regio een belangrijke rol om jeugdigen een thuis te bieden. Wanneer residentiële jeugdhulp toch noodzakelijk is, willen we dat dit deel uitmaakt van een ambulant traject: tijdelijk en gericht op zo snel mogelijk terug naar thuis. Binnen residentieel verblijf wordt een veilig en positief leefklimaat én maatwerk geboden. We zetten maximaal in op het voorkomen van verhuizingen. Dit heeft een groot ontwrichtend effect op jongeren. In de Hervormingsagenda is het belang van zo thuis mogelijk opgroeien voor jeugdigen opnieuw onderstreept. items.titel: A harmonized individual-level phytoplankton trait dataset from Mediterranean and Black Sea transitional waters
items.samenvatting_bron: Transitional waters are dynamic coastal ecosystems located at the interface between freshwater and marine environments. They are characterized by pronounced environmental variability resulting from the interaction between geomorphology, freshwater inputs, tidal exchanges, climatic variability, and human activities. These factors generate high habitat heterogeneity and complex ecological dynamics. Phytoplankton communities inhabiting transitional waters are particularly sensitive to both natural gradients and anthropogenic pressures, often exhibiting marked spatial and seasonal patterns in species composition, abundance and functional structure. In response to fluctuating environmental conditions, phytoplankton taxa display a wide range of morphometric and functional adaptations, making trait-based approaches especially suitable for investigating community organization and ecosystem functioning in these ecosystems. Although a large amount of phytoplankton trait data is available, its use could be enhanced through improved data harmonization and interoperability. The availability of FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable) phytoplankton trait data from transitional waters, coupled with associated environmental information, is therefore essential to support comparative analyses and to improve our understanding of trait–environment relationships in these vulnerable ecosystems. items.titel: Beyond channel count: metrological performance metrics for compact multi-channel spectral sensors
items.samenvatting_bron: Compact multi-channel spectral sensors based on thin-film interference filters offer a low-cost, integrable alternative to dispersive spectrometers, yet their performance is too often assessed by channel count alone, an indicator blind to inter-channel crosstalk, filter bandwidth, and the underdetermined nature of the spectral measurement. We present a metrological framework that formalises the channel-wise measurement model, identifies the dominant Type B instrumental uncertainty contributions (interference-filter centre-wavelength tolerance, responsivity line-shape deviation, PGA gain tolerance, and ADC quantisation and noise), and propagates them from the digital-count domain to irradiance through the device calibration curve. From the same datasheet parameters, the framework derives two figures of merit: the inter-channel crosstalk matrix C and the effective number of independent measurements Meff, obtained as the participation ratio of the eigenvalues of C. items.titel: Integrating temperature and CO2-concentration impact on crops into an input–output framework
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Environmental Input–Output Analysis (IOA) incorporates feedbacks in coupled economic-environmental systems, driven by an exogenous demand and fixed input–output coefficients with a linearity assumption. For some environmental problems, or over longer time periods, the IO coefficients and exogenous drivers may change. Here, we introduce a climate-feedback into an IO system via the crop sector to illustrate the potential couplings between climate change and material and economic flows. We use existing climate impact ensembles to calibrate climate feedback parameters for crop productivity and implement them in an expanded IO system. We generally find that the same exogenous demand can be met with lower output due to yield improvements, driven by the beneficial effect of CO 2 fertilization which generally dominates the modelled temperature effect on yield, essentially indicating a reduction in land-use intensity driven by CO2 fertilization. However, the temperature effect, which is positive or negative dependent on region, may be underestimated because of the inability of existing process-based models to simulate climate-related agricultural impacts. items.titel: Feasibility study of using magnetic and thermoelectric methods for the assessment of storage-induced changes in flux-cored welding wires
items.samenvatting_bron: The lack of knowledge regarding whether a welding consumable remains suitable for the welding process or has undergone degradation that precludes its further use constitutes a significant challenge. Appropriate control procedures and effective evaluation methods may contribute to addressing this issue. This study presents the results of investigations concerning the applicability of magnetic and thermoelectric methods for such an assessment. Rutile flux-cored welding wires were stored in four different locations and subsequently collected for testing after 3, 6, and 12 months. Their suitability for industrial application was initially assessed on the basis of visual examination. Subsequently, measurements of thermoelectric power, characterization of bulk magnetic properties, and Magnetic Barkhausen Noise (MBN) were performed for each wire. Visual inspection confirmed the good surface condition of the wires despite the exceedance of the recommended limits of temperature and relative humidity during storage. Competitive coordination of Cu and Sn with 2‐aminoterephthalic acid (H 2 BDC‐NH 2 ) is associated with altered precursor growth and a heterogeneous local environment, favoring the formation of defective SnO x domains during thermal conversion while enabling ligand‐derived nitrogen sites to anchor redistributed Cu species. Spectroscopic investigations reveal that the optimized Cu‐SnO x /NC catalyst contains abundant vacancy‐related SnO x environments and predominantly isolated Cu–N configurations, which are associated with stabilized O‐bound * OCHO intermediates and mitigated cathodic reconstruction of SnO x . Operando Raman spectroscopy further indicates persistent formate‐related intermediates and comparatively lower bicarbonate accumulation during CO 2 electroreduction. Consequently, Cu‐SnO x /NC achieves a formate Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 96% at −100 mA cm −2 and maintains efficiencies above 85% over a moderate current density range in both alkaline and neutral electrolytes. items.titel: Magnetically Induced Functional Fe 3 O 4 /Iron Foam Catalysts for Enhanced CO 2 ‐Assisted Ethane Dehydrogenation
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT CO 2 ‐assisted ethane dehydrogenation (CO 2 ‐EDH) combines olefin production with CO 2 conversion, yet suffers from high temperatures and catalyst instability in thermal catalysis. This work establishes an alternating current magnetic field (ACMF)‐mediated catalytic system using Fe 3 O 4 decorated on iron foam (Fe 3 O 4 /IF) as the induction catalyst, achieving significant enhancement of the CO 2 ‐EDH process under mild conditions. At 500°C, a temperature 200°C lower than that required in conventional thermal catalysis to reach a comparable conversion level, the system realized an ethane conversion of 22.2% with 97% ethylene selectivity. At an equivalent conversion level, the catalyst stability was improved by 15‐fold compared to traditional thermal catalysis, with continuous stable operation for 80 h. The eddy current effect induced by the alternating magnetic field promotes electron transfer between Fe and Fe 3 O 4 and accelerates the oxygen redox cycle, thereby enhancing the reaction kinetics of the CO 2 ‐EDH process based on the Mars–van Krevelen (MvK) mechanism. This work provides an effective approach for improving the performance of alkane dehydrogenation under mild conditions and contributes new insights to the field of magnetically induced catalysis.

Here, we combine biochemical and structural characterization with directed evolution of PsGalOx from Pseudarthrobacter siccitolerans. Spectroscopic analysis showed that PsGalOx can form the catalytically competent Cu(II)–tyrosyl radical state. The enzyme also displays an unusual modular architecture comprising two tandem carbohydrate-binding modules (CBMs). The enzyme preferentially oxidizes d-galactose and d-galactose-containing oligo- and polysaccharides. Functional analyses reveal distinct roles for the two CBM32 domains: CBM32-I enhances polysaccharide binding but limits soluble expression, whereas CBM32-II primarily contributes to protein stability. During directed evolution with d-galactose, recombination between the homologous CBMs generated chimeric single-CBM variants enriched primarily through increased soluble production rather than intrinsic catalytic improvement. Subsequent screening with benzyl alcohol as a model noncarbohydrate substrate selected second-shell substitutions near the copper center that increased intrinsic catalytic turnover and broadened substrate scope. items.titel: Efficient Separation of Xe/Kr by Induced Polarization on Single‐Atom Modified Ti 3 C 2 O 2 : A DFT Study
items.samenvatting_bron: The efficient separation of radioactive xenon (Xe) and krypton (Kr) is challenging due to their similar sizes and chemical inertness. To address this, dispersing metal atoms as single sites on a substrate can utilize their highly localized electronic structure and concentrated charge to enhance polarization of noble gas atoms, thereby achieving effective Xe/Kr adsorption and separation. Two‐dimensional MXene materials, with their large specific surface areas and tunable surface terminal groups, offer promising substrates for supporting metal atoms. In this study, we performed ab initio density functional theory (DFT) calculations to systematically evaluate the adsorption and separation capabilities of transition metal (TM) functionalized Ti 3 C 2 O 2 (TM‐Ti 3 C 2 O 2 ) for Xe and Kr. Among the tested metals, Cu–Ti 3 C 2 O 2 exhibited the strongest adsorption toward both gases. Charge density difference and partial density of states analyses revealed that the supported Cu atom induce significant polarization of Xe and Kr, facilitating pronounced interactions between the p orbitals of the gas atoms and the d orbitals of Cu. Furthermore, Cu–Ti 3 C 2 O 2 showed the largest difference in adsorption energy between Xe and Kr, demonstrating its strong potential as an effective material for Xe/Kr separation.

The results indicated that 98.64% of the MB dye had been removed. The model validation results showed 98.13%, indicating an excellent fit between the predicted and actual values. items.titel: γ‐Radionuclide Technetium‐99M Activated Long‐Lasting Chemodynamic Therapy and Immunogenic Brachytherapy for Enhanced Antitumor Immunity
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT Chemodynamic therapy (CDT) and brachytherapy face critical challenges, particularly the limited efficiency of Fenton reaction and the insufficient antitumor immunogenicity of brachytherapy. In this study, we employ the metal–organic framework nanocomposite Hf‐TCPP@Fe‐ 99m Tc (where TCPP = tetrakis(4‐carboxyphenyl) porphyrin and 99m Tc = technetium‐99m) for synergistic long‐lasting CDT and immunogenic brachytherapy. Benefiting from the robust interaction between 99m Tc‐emitted γ‐rays and the high‐Z element Hf, the secondary electrons generated during brachytherapy not only damage tumor cells but also establish an electron‐rich microenvironment that drives the continuous reduction of Fe 3+ to Fe 2+ , thereby sustaining a highly efficient Fenton reaction. With the generation of hydroxyl radical persisting for over 12 h, this synergistic effect reduced cell viability by an additional 28.6% beyond projections, thereby inducing effective immunogenic cell death, activating a systemic antitumor immune response, and inhibiting both primary and metastatic triple‐negative breast cancer. Through rational design, this work demonstrates that clinically prevalent nontherapeutic γ‐radionuclide can activate long‐lasting CDT and immunogenic brachytherapy to enhance antitumor immunogenicity.

A Comprehensive Review and Future Prospects of Aluminum–Sulfur Batteries: From Material Design to Practical Challenges
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT Aluminum–sulfur (Al–S) batteries are promising next‐generation energy storage systems owing to the high abundance, low cost, and multi‐electron redox capability of Al, combined with the high theoretical capacity and environmental friendliness of S. This review systematically compares the dual electrochemical mechanisms based on S reduction (S 0 /S 2− ) and S oxidation (S 0 /S 4+ ), highlighting their distinct advantages in energy density and safety. Key strategies for cathode design—including carbon‐based, anchoring‐functional, and catalytic‐functional hosts—are discussed, alongside electrolyte engineering using ionic liquids, deep eutectic solvents, inorganic molten salts, and aqueous systems. Recent advances in dendrite suppression, anode protective layers, and functional separators are also summarized. A central challenge identified is the sluggish Al 3+ solvation/desolvation kinetics, which limits rate capability and low‐temperature performance. The application of in situ/operando characterization techniques (XANES, Raman, UV–vis) to unravel complex reaction pathways is emphasized. By integrating multidisciplinary innovations, this review provides a comprehensive perspective and a phased commercialization roadmap, aiming to accelerate the transition of Al–S batteries from laboratory research to practical green energy storage.

items.titel: Microplastic contamination in agricultural systems: impacts on plant productivity, economic losses, and supply chain resilience
items.samenvatting_bron: Microplastics (MPs) have transitioned from a predominantly marine concern to a defining threat facing terrestrial agroecosystems, where croplands now function as one of the largest global reservoirs of plastic particles. This review synthesizes evidence to construct an integrated narrative that links the entry of MPs into farmland with declining plant productivity, quantifiable economic losses, and the erosion of agricultural supply chain resilience. The synthesis is based on a documented search of Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar covering January 2018 to March 2026, with explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria reported in Section 1.1. Sources, fate and soil-phase processes are treated in condensed form, because they are already covered comprehensively elsewhere; we retain only the evidence that propagates into crop, economic and supply-chain outcomes. Building on these soil-level disturbances, we evaluate the phytotoxic consequences for crops, spanning inhibited germination, impaired root architecture, reduced photosynthetic efficiency, disrupted nutrient acquisition, and the uptake and translocation of nano-sized particles into edible tissues. A central contribution of this review is the explicit coupling of these biophysical impacts to their economic and systemic dimensions, because recent global meta-analyses estimate that MP-induced photosynthetic suppression alone may reduce staple crop production by tens to hundreds of millions of tons annuall

items.titel: Development and application of an analytical method for the quantification of tire wear in atmospheric deposition
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract. Tire wear particles (TWP) are a major source of microplastic pollution and a carrier of rubber additives and metal-containing compounds that can be released into the environment and adversely affect ecosystems. Reliable quantification of TWP remains challenging because tire materials are compositionally heterogeneous and environmental samples contain complex organic and inorganic matrices that interfere with their analysis. Here, we present a pyrolysis-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (Py-GC-MS) method for the quantification of TWP in atmospheric deposition samples. The method combines targeted sample pretreatment, including density separation and removal of organic matrix components, with the analysis of six characteristic pyrolysis products of tire rubber, namely butadiene, 4-vinylcyclohexene, isoprene, limonene, styrene, and α-methylstyrene. The sum of the integrated peak areas of these markers is used to quantify TWP mass. Instrumental parameters, including pyrolysis temperature (set to 500 °C) and gas chromatographic separation, were systematically optimized to maximize sensitivity, reproducibility, and chromatographic resolution. Calibration was established using cryo-milled tread materials from 23 used passenger car and truck/bus tires as well as a mixture of cryo-milled tread materials representative of the U.S. tire market. The sum of the six marker signals showed a strong linear relationship with tire tread mass across different tire types (r² = 0.93).

items.titel: Regulation strategies of atom economy for iron-based catalysts in syngas catalytic conversion
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract As a key evaluation metric for direct catalytic syngas conversion, hydrogen atom economy or carbon atom economy can accurately quantify the different atom flows during the main and side reactions, which would provide new insight for the rational design. This work reviewed the active phase types, structural evolution patterns, and regulatory mechanisms for syngas conversion on iron-based catalysts. On this basis, it elaborated the optimization paths of carbon and hydrogen atom economies and analyzed the coupling and trade-offs. It was pointed out that the balance of hydrogen atom economy and carbon atom economy was the goal for improving the atomic utilization efficiency in iron-based catalytic syngas conversion. Moreover, the appropriate application of interdisciplinary strategies could open up new perspectives for the efficient regulation of atom economy and provide novel insights for developing high-performance catalytic systems.

items.titel: Pyrolysis temperature controls the accessible pore volume and capric acid encapsulation efficiency of coconut shell biochar
items.samenvatting_bron: Waste-derived biochar is a low-cost scaffold for shape-stabilized phase change materials (PCMs), yet how pyrolysis temperature governs the pore volume a molten PCM can reach remains unresolved. Here we decouple surface area from pore accessibility by preparing ZnCl 2 -activated coconut shell biochars at 550, 700, 850 and 1000 °C under an identical protocol and impregnating them with capric acid. Contrary to the assumption that higher BET surface area guarantees greater PCM loading, encapsulation efficiency tracks the pore volume accessible on the adsorption branch. Between the 850 and 1000 °C biochars the BET area differs by only 3.3%, whereas the BJH adsorption cumulative pore volume differs by 17.6% (0.1102 versus 0.1296 cm 3 g –1 ) and the encapsulation efficiency by 18.5% (57.59 versus 68.25%). High-resolution TEM resolves the origin: short, curved graphene fringes constrict pore entrances at 850 °C, whereas extended parallel stacks bound open channels at 1000 °C. Efficiency rises from 42.25% at 550 °C to 68.25% at 1000 °C; the optimized composite delivers 112.88 J g –1 , does not leak at 55 °C and retains 99% of its latent heat after 500 cycles. Accessible pore volume, not surface area, is the key design criterion for biochar PCMs in passive building thermal regulation.

Results revealed that Northern China functioned as a net soil carbon source over the 30-year interval, losing approximately 0.56 Gt of SOC and 0.56 Gt of SIC. Land use type emerged as the dominant control on carbon source-sink patterns. Grassland transitioned into strong carbon sources driven primarily by SIC losses of 1.51 Gt, whereas unutilized land exhibited estimated net carbon gains with apparent SIC accumulation of 2.06 Gt. Beyond altering carbon stocks, land use change reversed regional source-sink patterns and markedly heightened the sensitivity of soil carbon dynamics to environmental changes with explanatory strength increment of 0.11 for SOC and 0.09 for SIC, respectively. items.titel: Design of a monolithic cellulose Janus-like membrane for oil/water separation
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Janus membranes offer a good solution for oil/water mixtures due to their opposite wettability, but existing designs often suffer from limitations arising from complex, resource-intensive fabrication procedures. The membrane retains excellent mechanical robustness (3.50 MPa), with a breaking force of 5.23 N, withstanding repeated deformations including axial rolling, compression, and bending, without cracking or delamination. items.titel: Low-Frequency Magnetic Field Mitigation Using Recyclable Sintered Pure-Iron Powder Compacts for Safer Power and Sensor Infrastructure
items.samenvatting_bron: High-current carrying conductors, electrical machines, power-electronic systems, and sensors generate low-frequency magnetic fields that can cause electromagnetic interference and may result in higher magnetic-field exposure in occupied or sensitive environments. This study proposes a new low frequency shielding material in the form of sintered pure-iron powder compacts as an alternative to the conventional high-permeability magnetic shielding alloys. This material is manufactured by following controlled environment annealing, green compaction and sintering of high purity iron powder. The magnetic properties of the compacted specimen were determined by characterization according to IEC 60404-4 standard, and scanning electron microscopy was used to study the microstructural features, and chemical analysis was performed by using energy dispersive spectroscopy to validate purity of the iron powder. Experimentally determined magnetic properties were used in finite element simulations to evaluate the shielding performance when different shielding geometries manufactured from the proposed material are placed around a current-carrying conductor. Analysis was done when the conductor carries current of 1000 Amp with focus to evaluate different shielding topologies, including open, square, hexagonal and circular shapes. items.titel: Study On Environmental Impact Due To Brick Industries. A Case Study In Chandragiri Municipality
items.samenvatting_bron: The brick manufacturing industry is one of the leading contributors to environmental degradation in peri-urban Nepal, yet site-specific assessments at the municipal level remain limited. items.titel: Male cone development in Ginkgo biloba uncovers recurrent reproductive modules partially shared with Cycas circinalis
items.samenvatting_bron: The origin of seed plants transformed land plant reproduction by protecting the embryo and enabling dispersal across diverse ecosystems. items.titel: A renaissance of pseudosands: on improving the understanding of soil architecture in deeply weathered soils
items.samenvatting_bron: Soil texture, the most widely used soil property to describe single grain size distribution, is different from soil structure. Setting them equal neglects the impact of actual particle arrangements under natural conditions. Particularly in deeply weathered soils, the mismatch between soil texture and structure has widely been described. An initial literature review revealed a persistent lack of consistent classification for pseudosands, hindering comparison across studies. items.titel: Positively Charged Hollow Fiber Nanofiltration Membrane With an SPSf / PEI Bilayer Prepared via Dip‐Coating
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT Nanofiltration (NF) has attracted considerable interest in water purification and resource recovery. Hollow fiber membranes offer high packing density, large surface‐area‐to‐volume ratio, and low‐pressure high‐flux operation. However, the fabrication of hollow fiber NF membranes often suffers from non‐uniform and discontinuous separation layers, while most conventional NF membranes are negatively charged and inclined to fouling caused by the adsorption of positively charged ions. In this work, a positively charged hollow fiber NF membrane was fabricated by constructing a sulfonated polysulfone (SPSf)/polyethyleneimine (PEI) electrostatic assembly bilayer via dip‐coating. The SPSf interlayer was first coated onto the polyethersulfone (PES) surface to enhance interfacial adhesion, facilitate PEI assembly, and prevent excessive PEI penetration into the membrane pores, thereby forming a dense, defect‐free selective layer via electrostatic interactions. The PES/SPSf‐PEI membrane showed high rejection for MgCl 2 (90.96%), crystal violet (99.56%), and rhodamine B (99.81%). Moreover, a flux recovery ratio of 86.77% was achieved after three fouling‐cleaning cycles using rhodamine B as a model foulant. This work provides a facile and controllable approach for preparing high‐performance positively charged hollow fiber NF membranes, showing great potential for divalent cation rejection and dye treatment.

In a wound‐associated infection model, topical application of CSC@PTQ10‐SY1 significantly reduces bacterial burden and inflammation, resulting in improved wound healing outcomes compared to the control group. items.titel: Massively Multiplexed Photonic Chip With Cross‐Channel Fusion For Harmonized Biosensing
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT Accurate, label‐free analysis of complex biological mixtures is limited by poor multiplexing scalability and inconsistent responses across sensor samples. We introduce a transformative sensing platform that integrates large‐scale photonic multiplexing with data‐driven analytics to overcome these constraints. Our modular, affordable glass‐chip whispering–gallery–mode (WGM) photonic architecture is designed to support simultaneous readout of up to 100 sensing channels comprising over 10 000 high‐Q microresonators, exceeding existing multiplexing capabilities by more than two orders of magnitude. The photonic system is reinforced by the novel, cross‐platform, deep learning framework BioCCF. It applies cross‐channel fusion in biosensing for the first time and enables harmonized operation across heterogeneous chips by leveraging domain adaptation. Using over 200 h of measurements from nine independent chips, we demonstrate chip‐independent multiplexed biosensing with 99.3% identification accuracy and relative quantification errors of 10 for immunoglobulin G mixtures. Beyond this validation, the platform supports multi‐analyte immunoassays, environmental monitoring, and distributed diagnostics, enabling aligned sensor networks with shared data infrastructures and continuously improving generalization of the common analyzing framework.

items.titel: A harmonized database of biosphere–atmosphere ammonia flux measurements across ecosystems and pollution regimes
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Ammonia (NH 3 ) is a trace gas with detrimental effects on human health and ecosystems. Understanding and quantification of NH 3 exchange between the biosphere and atmosphere is essential for assessing ecosystem nitrogen budgets and critical load exceedances. Yet, uncertainty in these processes remains significant, due to the global scarcity of measurements. We created a database of more than 40,000 records of NH 3 flux measurements across ecosystems, including heathlands, peatlands, grasslands, forests, croplands, and dunes, in areas with varying ambient NH 3 and sulphur dioxide concentrations, using different measurement techniques from 1991 to 2024. A significant share of measurements originates from the Netherlands, reflecting its early deployment of a high-resolution NH 3 monitoring network. Fluxes are quality controlled and harmonized using consistent algorithms, with uncertainty estimates included. Fluxes were recalculated using consistent stability correction functions, ensuring comparability across sites. By providing this database, we aim to contribute to the understanding of the NH 3 biosphere-atmosphere exchange, its environmental controls, the validation and calibration of NH 3 exchange schemes, and the characterization of NH 3 fluxes across ecosystems.

Contested urbanisms: The politics of heritage and housing in Jakarta’s kampungs
items.samenvatting_bron: Do heritage-making projects resist or advance gentrification in Southeast Asia? We find that invasion-associated losses of functional α diversity and functional shifts toward acquisitive strategies, reduce species asynchrony and species stability, respectively. These changes ultimately lead to lower temporal stability at the local scale (α stability). Meanwhile, invasion-associated functional shifts toward acquisitive seed dispersal strategies weaken functional β diversity, which reduces asynchrony community dynamics among local communities (spatial asynchrony). These concurrent declines in α stability and spatial asynchrony collectively destabilize metacommunity-scale stability. Within established plantations, conserving and restoring riparian margins can reduce erosion, improve connectivity, and support biodiversity. The Riparian Ecosystem Restoration in Tropical Agriculture (RERTA) Project is a long-term Before-After Control-Impact experiment established within oil palm plantations in Riau, Indonesia, to evaluate alternative riparian restoration strategies following plantation replanting. items.titel: Protected-area-based nature-based governance and green-blue infrastructure-to-built conversion: spatial regression discontinuity evidence from Kinmen National Park, Taiwan
items.samenvatting_bron: Nature-based solutions (NbS) and green-blue infrastructure (GBI) are increasingly promoted for sustainable built environments, yet boundary-based evidence on specific land-conversion mechanisms remains limited. GBI-to-built conversion (G2B) is the primary outcome; strict built-up change, developed-land change, Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) change, and GBI fragmentation are contrasting or secondary outcomes. The main G2B coefficient is −0.00188, equivalent to a 0.19-percentage-point lower conversion share immediately inside the boundary and about 19% of the raw outside-sample mean as a descriptive benchmark. Heteroskedasticity-robust and robust bias-corrected RD inference support a negative discontinuity, but the 60 m donut specification and Conley spatial-HAC corrections weaken statistical precision. No robust discontinuity is found for strict built-up expansion. External distance bands show positive dBuilt and G2B signals in the outer 600–1,000 m belt, interpreted as spatially associated peripheral development pressure rather than park-caused displacement. Among these, endophytic fungi play a crucial role in enhancing host plant growth and stress tolerance. Halophytes host a diverse community of endophytic fungi that are naturally adapted to extreme saline and arid environments. These fungi establish symbiotic associations with their host plants, improving plant performance and contributing to ecosystem services, thereby making them valuable for sustainable agriculture and environmental management. In agricultural systems, these endophytes promote plant growth and yield by producing phytohormones, solubilizing nutrients, and activating stress-protective pathways. They further enhance tolerance to salinity and drought by maintaining ion homeostasis and stimulating antioxidant defence mechanisms. Several halophyte-associated fungi, including members of the genera Fusarium, Chaetomium , and Penicillium , have been reported to exhibit biocontrol potential through the production of antimicrobial metabolites that suppress plant pathogens. items.titel: From tourist-perceived authenticity to storytelling tendency: the mediating role of well-being in agricultural heritage tourism
items.samenvatting_bron: Authenticity links tourist experiences with narrative communication in agricultural heritage tourism. Drawing on the Cognition–Affect–Behavior framework, this study models the relationships among perceived authenticity, well-being, and storytelling tendency. Data from 402 visitors to Hongcun, Chengkan, and Xixinan in Anhui, China, were analyzed using PLS-SEM. The results show that perceived authenticity comprises ecological experience, cultural interaction, heritage reminiscence, personal reflection, and continuity of tradition. Cultural interaction has a significant indirect effect only through psychological well-being, while neither indirect pathway involving personal reflection is significant. These findings provide a theoretical basis for conserving living heritage and communicating heritage values in traditional villages.

items.titel: Land Use Change, Spillovers, and Transitions: Global Trends, Prospects, and Emerging Drivers
items.samenvatting_bron: In this review, we first compile data on global trends and rates of major land use changes over the recent decades, and summarize the main insights revealed by these data. We then review recent research and quantitative estimates on key land use spillover processes, i.e., leakage, indirect land use change, rebound effect and land sparing, and agglomeration economies. We then turn to the prospective, by highlighting a few recent processes that may have an increasingly important influence on land use dynamics, and synthesizing recent quantitative projections of global land use dynamics until 2050, discussing business as usual (BAU) trends as well as more transformative scenarios. Extracting high-level lessons from previous research on land use transitions, we bring these different lines of evidence together to synthesize general conclusions about global land use dynamics and how to enhance sustainability through land use.

items.titel: The gradual institutionalisation of the reflexive approach in governmental evaluation systems
items.samenvatting_bron: While transformation-focused evaluation is thriving in theory, less attention has been paid to how such approaches become institutionalised in governmental evaluation systems. We suggest further inquiry and debate on the drivers behind the opening up of conceptions of what evaluation is and should achieve in the wider governance system.

items.titel: Capability or participation? A dimensional analysis of ocean digital twins and its implications for maritime spatial planning governance
items.samenvatting_bron: Ocean digital twins, Digital Twins of the Ocean (DTOs), are increasingly promoted as the decision-support backbone for marine spatial planning (MSP), yet the term denotes at least four incompatible conceptions across communities that rarely cite one another, alongside a critical strand that interrogates the object rather than advancing a conception of it, and most marine decision-support tools are never adopted in practice. This paper asks whether, and how, a DTO can serve participatory marine governance. Using a concept-centric morphological analysis, we assemble a corpus of eleven DTO conceptions, one critical reading of the field, and fifteen deployed systems and decision-support tools, and code each against six dimensions derived from the literature: three graded (scope, capability, coupling) and three categorical (object, purpose, intended users); the full coding matrix is provided as supplementary material. Mapping the corpus reveals a structured capability–participation trade-off rather than a uniform spread: the conceptions richest in analytical capability address the narrowest set of users, while those reaching non-expert stakeholders sit lowest on the capability ladder; no continuously synchronised system combines both, and only an aspirational programme (DITTO) claims to. Because MSP is a stakeholder-driven governance process that demands both, this trade-off diagnoses why capable ocean twins go unused in planning. Setting the framework against the stages of the pl

items.titel: Macroevolutionary insights into the range limits of species and lineages
items.samenvatting_bron: Understanding the intrinsic and extrinsic factors that determine the range limits of species is an important goal in biology. Much work has focused on understanding the range limits of populations and individual species, whereas the factors that determine the distributions of evolutionary lineages have received less attention in the range limits literature. In this review I highlight recent macroscale insights into the range limits of flowering plant lineages, and briefly compare these to findings from other taxa. Although life on Earth has managed to adapt to practically all environments, recent methodological and analytical advances in macroevolution and biogeography show that adaptation to novel environments is relatively rare: multiple large-scale studies estimate that well over 80% of speciation events are confined within their ancestral macroclimatic environment, or biome. This high degree of phylogenetic biome conservatism reflects that Earth is crossed by various major environmental adaptive barriers, or hard range limits, that strongly constrain the ranges of both species and lineages. These adaptive barriers differ significantly in how often they are surmounted: some barriers, like fire, are crossed relatively frequently, whereas others, such as frost or salinity, delimit species' ranges over many millions of years. Some barriers thus structure the global distribution of terrestrial lineages more stringently than oceans between landmasses. Furthermore, broad congrue

items.titel: Antibiotic production reduces the cost of resource exploitation in Streptomyces coelicolor
items.samenvatting_bron: Soil is a competitive environment containing a variety of resources used for bacterial growth. Complex polysaccharides, like chitin or starch, require the secretion of enzymes that degrade these resources into smaller units before they can be consumed. However, exoenzymes and the products they create are public goods, meaning they can be used by competitors who consume and benefit from these public goods even if they do not produce enzymes themselves. Here, we test the hypothesis that antibiotics produced by Streptomyces are used to privatize public goods by restricting access to resource exploiters. Using experiments with Streptomyces coelicolor and Bacillus subtilis, we first show that B. subtilis resource exploitation significantly reduces S. coelicolor fitness on a complex resource (starch) but not on a simple carbon source (maltose) which does not require exoenzyme secretion. Next, we show that antibiotics produced by S. coelicolor markedly increase fitness against resource exploiters, despite evidence that antibiotic production is metabolically costly. Finally, we find that the benefits of antibiotic production and the costs of resource exploitation are both higher during growth on lower resource concentrations. Our results provide insights into the context-dependent costs and benefits of antibiotic secretion in Streptomyces and highlight the role of resource complexity and concentration in mediating competitive strategies in bacteria.

items.titel: Enabling global prediction of marsh vegetation survival during extreme storms
items.samenvatting_bron: Flood protection by coastal vegetated systems depends on the persistence of vegetation structures, but it is currently impossible to predict vegetation survival during extreme storms. Using the largest artificially generated waves in the world, we here quantified the persistence of tidal marsh vegetation by measuring stem breakage of winter-state vegetation (3 species and mimics) during extreme storms with up to 2.0 m significant wave height, 4 m water level and 8 s peak period waves. Vegetation persistence was unexpectedly high, with on average only 30% biomass loss. Stiff stems which were unable to sway under waves were most frequently broken, so the storm left behind a more flexible and resilient post-storm canopy. We derived a generic diagram to predict biomass loss of global vegetation species across increasing storm intensities, allowing prediction of marsh vegetation survival under extreme storm events – a critical next step towards reducing the uncertainty hampering the implementation of nature-based flood protection strategies. Tidal marsh vegetation withstands extreme storms with only 30% average biomass loss, as flexible stems survive better than rigid ones, based on experiments using waves up to 2 m high and a predictive framework for vegetation survival.

items.titel: Sustainability negotiated: Relational constellations of farmers’ practices across personal, interpersonal, and systemic spheres
items.samenvatting_bron: Farmers' engagement with sustainability often remains implicit, embedded in everyday practices, social relations, and responses to institutional pressures. This study makes these implicit negotiations visible by examining how farmers in Flevoland (the Netherlands) navigate sustainability through the dynamic interplay of three spheres of influence: personal, interpersonal, and systemic. Advancing relational sustainability scholarship, we move beyond explanations that locate sustainability either in individual attitudes (‘inner worlds’) or in structural constraints (‘outer worlds’) by empirically operationalising their co-constitution in situated farming realities. Drawing on interviews and participant observation with 32 farmers, we identified seven recurrent aspects of sustainability talk and practice, organised across the three spheres. Through systematic cross-case comparison, we found six relational constellations: recurrent configurations of spheres that express distinct relational logics through which farmers perceive and prioritise sustainability, varying from value-driven integration and socially anchored commitment to strategic pragmatism and systemic contestation. These constellations show that sustainability is neither a stable attribute of individuals nor a property of systems, but an emergent, negotiated orientation shaped by shifting alignments between convictions, social relations, and systemic structures. items.titel: Navigating Post-Growth Planning
items.samenvatting_bron: Spatial planning faces mounting challenges with regard to land use, housing, energy, and infrastructure – fields where traditional solutions, such as expanding land use, are no longer viable or desirable. Planning’s fundamental assumptions of temporal certainty, linear control, and clear roles erode and demand fundamental rethinking. This paper connects post-growth planning to complexity theory to navigate this tension by emphasising adaptivity, reflexivity, and normativity. Drawing on Niklas Luhmann’s systems theory, the exploration reveals how spatial planning’s self-images and roles reproduce growth-dependent actions despite mounting evidence of their unsustainability. It uses insights, especially with regard to land use, as well as podcast interviews with key thinkers to transcend these lock-ins by embracing ‘intentional unintentionality’. In so doing it deliberately reshapes one’s own roles while acknowledging the non-linear, unpredictable effects on external systems. The transformative potential lies not in top-down control but in planning’s capacity to generate alternatives from within; leveraging complexity to align with post-growth priorities.

items.titel: Climate Change Disinformation| Unraveling Debunked Climate Change Disinformation and Responses to Fact-Checks: Evidence From the United States, Netherlands, and Philippines
items.samenvatting_bron: Although climate change skepticism and denialism have been considered influential narratives in the contemporary digital information landscape, we know little about how such narratives are legitimized in climate change disinformation across different national settings. Against this background, this study relies on an in-depth qualitative content analysis of fact-checked disinformation in the Netherlands, the United States, and the Philippines as contrasting global cases. In addition, to explore the level of resistance to fact-checks, social media comments in response to fact-checking information were analyzed inductively. Our main findings indicate that climate skepticism was often constructed by deceptively re-interpreting, de-contextualizing, delegitimizing, or altering expert knowledge and scientific evidence. Disinformation claims and responses often used a populist logic, for which common sense and direct observations were juxtaposed to the alleged dishonesty of scientists. Responses to fact-checks mostly reinforced disinformation or challenged the fact-checker, which offers limited support for the real-life effectiveness of climate change debunks.

items.titel: Rights of nature in socio-legal perspective: from law to practice
items.samenvatting_bron: As the ecological crisis deepens, there is a growing call from lawyers and activists to revise the very foundations on which environmental law is built. One increasingly prominent proposal is to grant nature its own inherent rights. Lawmakers across the world have formally recognised rights of nature (RoN) and communities have started using rights language to nurture new relationships with nature. A thriving literature studies the socio-political dynamics underlying and emanating from this development. This paper reviews how this scholarship assesses the origins and impacts of such rights and lays out a research agenda for future inquiry. It identifies two dominant research paradigms and outlines a third, yet to be fully developed one. The first views RoN through the lens of contentious politics over their legal formalisation and enactment. The second situates them within (counter-)hegemonic discourses, probing their ability to disrupt entrenched ontologies. The third highlights how everyday practices interact with RoN. Rather than locating change in political victories or structural ruptures, this approach situates it in the endogenous shifts of routines in communities, movements, and organisations. The paper argues that dynamics of norm translation and routinisation can both reproduce but also resist dominant forms of governing nature.

extra.tijdschrift: The International Journal of Human Rights

items.titel: Greening cities to ensure biosphere functional integrity: Insights from Rotterdam and Lagos
items.samenvatting_bron: The Earth Commission has proposed that 20-25% of every square kilometre of managed lands, including in cities, be reserved for nature to ensure its local functioning and human wellbeing -biosphere functional integrity boundary (BFI). This research adopted a multi-method justice-oriented approach grounded in the Earth System Justice framework to assess the challenges and opportunities of implementing this proposed biosphere functional integrity boundary in Rotterdam and Lagos. We conclude: (a) This proposed scientific boundary precedes global policy but complements the EU's voluntary urban greening guidelines. (b) Good quality green is inequitably distributed in case study countries for different reasons. (c) Combining existing large-scale planning and subsidizing small-scale greening efforts should enable Rotterdam to achieve the boundary, despite risks of gentrification, inequitable access, and poor-quality green. For Lagos, development imperatives compete with existing greening. (d) This research has enhanced Earth system justice and its 9 criteria for just boundaries. We believe that adopting a contextually relevant BFI boundary may enable equitable distribution of good quality and accessible green especially for the people who need it most.

items.titel: Molecular phylogeny and updated classification of jewel damselflies (Odonata: Zygoptera: Chlorocyphidae)
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Chlorocyphidae (Odonata: Zygoptera) represent a family of odonates found in tropical Asia and Africa, composed of 162 species. The family is characterized by a pronounced snout-like clypeus, wings that usually extend beyond the abdomen, and striking male coloration correlated with elaborate courtship behavior. Morphological differences between species and among genera are limited. To date, there is no extensive phylogeny of the group. As a result, the current classification is primarily based on coloration and morphological features that have not been tested in a phylogenetic framework. Our taxon sampling includes 90 species (> 55% of diversity). We targeted 92 AHE genes to test previous hypotheses of chlorocyphid classification. We present an updated classification. We recover Chlorocyphidae as monophyletic and Cyrano as sister to the remaining genera. We describe two new subfamilies, increasing the number to six: Cyranoinae Fomekong-Lontchi, Kalkman and Bybee subfam. nov . and Indocyphinae Fomekong-Lontchi, Kalkman and Bybee subfam. nov . A total of 26 species are reclassified to another genus (highlighting the difficulty with Chlorocyphidae morphology and classification), of which 13 are placed in two newly described genera: Ebenocypha Fomekong-Lontchi, Kalkman and Bybee gen. nov . and Scapanocypha Fomekong-Lontchi, Kalkman and Bybee gen. nov . Also, the genera Melanocypha , Pachycypha , Sclerocypha , and Watuwila are synonymized with Libellago . This new classifi

items.titel: The atoll gap: area, governance, and the under-recognition of a major coral reef system
items.samenvatting_bron: Global assessments project widespread coral reef degradation under continued ocean warming and acidification, underscoring the urgent need to identify and account for the full diversity of coral reef systems within conservation planning. Atolls are dynamic reef-ocean-land systems whose persistence depends on coral reef sediment production, land-sea connectivity, and cross-ecosystem nutrient subsidies. Some atoll reef environments may also support coral assemblages with elevated thermal tolerance which could mean atolls are, and will increasingly be, important local-to-regional coral sources as global and local impacts continue to limit corals. Using a curated dataset of 310 Indo-Pacific atolls and high-resolution global coral reefscape mapping from the Allen Coral Atlas, we show that 309 Indo-Pacific atolls contain 27,211 km 2 of mapped shallow reefscape, representing 41.5% of all Indo-Pacific reef area and 7.8 percent of global mapped shallow reefscape area. This spatial accounting places Indo-Pacific atolls among the world’s major coral reefscape networks by area. We interpret this result alongside literature on atoll ecology, geomorphology, and governance to suggest that atoll-associated reefs merit more explicit consideration in Indo-Pacific coral reef conservation planning, while recognizing that additional comparative evidence on conservation finance, monitoring, protection, and governance would be needed to directly quantify under-recognition.

items.titel: Field or virtual? Perceived impact of academic excursions through the eyes of (future) hydrologists
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract. Field training such as excursions have always been an integral part of the education of geoscientists. The value of these excursions is frequently debated, related to the efforts and costs involved with their organization. Professionally prepared virtual excursions are sometimes presented as a possible alternative for field activities. This debate has been accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic: the lockdown forced teachers to come up with virtual and online education material, also for fieldwork and excursions. One of the courses at Wageningen University (the Netherlands) heavily affected by COVID-19 restrictions was the Master course Catchment and Climate Hydrology. An important and integral component of that course is an 8-day excursion to Iceland where relatively undisturbed catchments are studied in a country heavily affected by climate change. All students from the 2020 and 2021 cohort took the alternative professionally prepared virtual excursion. After the pandemic, in 2022, these students did get the offer to join an extra added excursion. About 50 % of that population was able to join. This configuration, involving student cohorts that participated only in the field excursion, only in the virtual excursion, or in both, provided an unique opportunity to assess student evaluations of field-based education and the potential of virtual alternatives. items.samenvatting_bron: Sophie Chao's 2025 monograph, Land of Famished Beings, which received the 2026 Mid-Career Book Prize from the Asian Studies Association of Australia, examines how Indigenous Marind communities understand and theorise hunger in lowland West Papua, a place where industrial plantation expansion and settler-colonial violence are radically reconfiguring ecologies, socialities, and identities (Figure 1).By centering Indigenous feminist theories of hunger, Chao offers new ways of thinking about the relationship between the environment, food, and nourishment in an age of self-consuming capitalist growth.She also considers how Indigenous theories invite anthropologists to reimagine the ethics and politics of ethnographic writing and the responsibilities, hesitations, and compromises that shape anthropological commitments in and beyond the field.In this book review forum, six scholars-Margaret Jolly, Shiori Shakuto, Hatib Kadir,

items.titel: Integrating ideals and urban datasets for sustainable city monitoring
items.samenvatting_bron: This study highlights the potential of connecting ideals and semantic web technology to overcome challenges in urban sustainability monitoring. City governments generally employ abstract concepts to communicate sustainability goals. Moreover, siloed monitoring systems are often used to track a multitude of metrics and indicators. However, the absence of an overarching strategy in cities’ monitoring frameworks and the incompatibility between various datasets and indicators can result in fragmented approaches. By using “Ideals”, actors can collaborate to achieve important objectives and share a unified understanding of the concepts employed. The authors propose the use of ideals to bridge different disciplines and achieve comprehensive insights through indicator-based monitoring systems. The City of Amsterdam is used as an exploratory case study to demonstrate how a domain ontology that combines the examination of coalition agreements, urban datasets, and monitoring systems can provide insights into how a city operationalizes and monitors its own interpretation of sustainable development.

items.titel: Aridity regulates scale-dependent effects of multiple resource additions on productivity stability in Eurasian grasslands
items.samenvatting_bron: Increasing the supply of multiple limiting resources generally reduces biodiversity and community stability in grasslands. Aridity is known to modify biodiversity-stability relationships, yet it remains unclear whether the effects of multiple resource supply on biodiversity and stability vary along aridity gradients and across spatial scales. Here, we examine how aridity mediates the responses of biodiversity and stability at multiple scales to increasing the number of added resources (e.g., water and nutrients) in Eurasian grasslands. Increasing the number of added resources reduced local plant species richness, asynchronous biomass dynamics among local communities (spatial asynchrony), and the stability of productivity at larger spatial scales, but had no effect on local-scale productivity stability. The negative effects of multiple resource addition on diversity, spatial asynchrony and large-scale productivity stability weakened with increasing aridity, with more arid grasslands showing weaker responses. Mechanistically, increasing resource supply reduced large-scale productivity stability primarily by reducing spatial asynchrony, while increasing aridity weakened the contribution of spatial asynchrony to large-scale productivity stability. Overall, our results demonstrate that the negative effects of multiple resource supply on grassland stability are scale-dependent and strongly regulated by aridity. items.titel: Is Evidence‐Based Policymaking an Environmental Studies Agenda? An Interpretive Review
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT Studies of knowledge development and use for public decision‐making can be found across the social sciences. There have been increasing calls for meaningful integration of the contrasting disciplinary perspectives on this topic, including from environmental and sustainability sciences. This paper provides a preliminary investigation of the feasibility of such an agenda by examining environmental studies of knowledge development and use, using an analytical framework derived from the policy sciences of evidence‐based policymaking. These two literatures have progressed in parallel for several decades, with just a subset of scholars working at their interface. The paper presents an interpretive systematic review of environmental studies to assess its conceptual coherence with the policy sciences. The literature survey indicates a schism between contrasting epistemologies, much like in policy sciences. Yet, most literature, regardless of epistemological orientation, demonstrates an appreciation of the complexities and contingencies of knowledge use for policymaking in ways that align well with interpretivist policy sciences. Environmental literatures are, however, pre‐occupied by science‐policy interfaces as the central locus of knowledge development and use, contrary to policy sciences' understanding of contemporary policy advisory systems. items.titel: Towards sustainable construction: A Roadmap for Aligning BES6001 with the UN SDGs
items.samenvatting_bron: The architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) sector has grown significantly over recent decades, sparking ongoing debate about its environmental impact. While advancing sustainability is essential, the sector’s role in meeting housing needs, upgrading infrastructure, and restoring biodiversity remains critical to delivering safe and resilient communities. Responsible sourcing and green supply chains are increasingly recognised as key mechanisms for delivering sustainable construction. BES6001 is a certification standard for responsible sourcing, offering a structured and transparent framework for AEC organisations producing materials. However, its potential contribution to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) remains insufficiently explored. This study examines the alignment between BES6001 and the SDGs, through the development of a conceptual roadmap. The roadmap was subject to expert review and identified strongest contributions to SDG-8 and SDG-12, although findings are based on preliminary validation (n=7). By analysing BES6001’s scoring criteria and principles, the roadmap illustrates how UK organisations may support the operationalisation of SDG commitments through BES6001 certification. Recommendations include revising BES6001 to strengthen SDG alignment and holistic review of SDG targets for developed regions where current goals may lack relevance. items.titel: Human-centred design approaches to tsunami mitigation under sea level rise in Kesennuma, Japan
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract. Human-centred design (HCD) is increasingly prioritised as studies show human experience is critical in infrastructure use, and recent policies call for more socially responsive design. Tsunami impacts intensify as sea level rise (SLR) raises baseline water levels and reduces existing defence effectiveness, yet HCD informed approaches are rarely tested under projected SLR. Based on identified infrastructure preferences in Kesennuma City, Japan, we develop three multi-layered defence configurations: an environmentally integrated eco hybrid system (Design 1), a discreet open feeling barrier system (Design 2), and a reinforced high-performance system (Design 3). Using TUNAMI-N2 numerical modelling, 150 simulations combine three tsunami sources, five SLR conditions, and five defence states. Results for inundation extent, fatality rates, and economic loss show a consistent hierarchy: Design 3 achieves the strongest containment, while Design 2, which more closely aligns with residents’ preferences for openness and access, delivers near equivalent reductions typically within 10–15 percent. Design 1 provides only limited hazard reduction and is unsuitable as a standalone mitigation system. We show that HCD informed configurations can deliver strong technical performance and support a shift toward socially integrated, multi-layered tsunami protection under rising sea levels.

items.titel: A theoretical model of co-production of public goods and services: A Systematic literature review and thematic synthesis
items.samenvatting_bron: This study examines the transformative role of co-production in delivering public goods and services across diverse public-service contexts. It aims to examine the nature, application, drivers, barriers, and reported outcomes of co-production. A systematic literature review with thematic synthesis was conducted using 10 peer-reviewed studies selected through predetermined eligibility criteria. The findings identified stakeholder engagement, knowledge integration, resource availability, and motivational drivers as recurring factors associated with effective co-production. The reviewed evidence indicates that co-production can facilitate citizen participation, knowledge exchange, service improvement, learning, and responsiveness to public needs. However, implementation can be constrained by unequal participation, power imbalances, limited financial and institutional resources, technological barriers, weak trust, and difficulties in consistently measuring outcomes. Based on the synthesis, the study develops the Integrated Co-Production Impact (ICI) Theory, which proposes that motivational drivers promote stakeholder engagement, engagement facilitates knowledge integration, and resource availability enables integrated knowledge to contribute to co-production effectiveness. items.titel: Structural diagnosis and evolution of urban resilience in dryland oasis urban agglomerations from an eco-immunological perspective
items.samenvatting_bron: Dryland oasis urban agglomerations face increasing drought risk, but gains in long-term adaptive capacity may not translate into stronger structural resilience because additive indices allow strong dimensions to offset weak ones. This study developed a partially non-compensatory four-dimensional super-trapezoid resilience model (TE4) integrating resistance, recovery, adaptive capacity, and institutional learning and preparedness, and applied it to ten city- and county-level units on the Northern Slope of the Tianshan Mountains during 2014–2024. The traditional composite index increased by 5.09% and adaptive capacity by 29.38% between the 2014 and 2024 endpoints, whereas the TE4 endpoint value in 2024 was 1.32% lower than that in 2014; however, its downward temporal trend was not statistically significant. Potential resilience rose by 9.28%, recovery capacity fell by 8.03%, and the unrealized resilience gap widened by 15.67%, indicating a modeled recovery-related conversion deficit. Removing NDVI-derived indicators barely altered TE4 rankings (Spearman’s ρ = 0.983). Panel models did not show short-term NPP buffering by higher TE4 under stronger drought, while pre-event recovery capacity showed the strongest positive but statistically inconclusive association with post-drought NPP recovery. TE4 is therefore a structural diagnostic tool for identifying capacity deficits and prioritizing recovery-oriented disaster risk reduction rather than a direct predictor of annual ecosystem

items.titel: Breaking Bioclimatic Boundaries: Behavioral Plasticity, Not Physiological Adaptation, Enables the Invasion of a Tropical Ant into Temperate China
items.samenvatting_bron: Biological invasions often challenge our understanding of climatic niches. Recently, the tropical ant Pheidole megacephala was discovered establishing overwintering populations in Beijing (39°N), significantly exceeding its predicted northern limit (28°N). We tested whether this range expansion is driven by rapid physiological adaptation or behavioral buffering. We integrated genetic analysis, physiological assays (CTmin), and microcosm experiments simulating nest excavation under cooling stress with artificial heat sources incorporated to mimic anthropogenic thermal refugia. Results showed that the Beijing populations originated from two distinct introduction events rather than a single cold-adapted lineage. Contrary to the adaptation hypothesis, we found no significant difference in CTmin between the Beijing (temperate) and Guangdong (subtropical) populations. Instead, field surveys linked nests closely to anthropogenic infrastructures, suggesting exploitation of artificial thermal refugia. Laboratory simulations confirmed that under cooling stress, ants actively utilized micro-heat sources. Under moderate cooling, attraction to micro-heat sources inhibited deep excavation, anchoring colonies in vulnerable shallow layers and potentially functioning as an ecological trap. However, during extreme cold, these same heat sources provided a vital survival buffer by maintaining motor function where ants in unheated environments perished. items.titel: Environmental excellence in Saudi Arabia: Governance, achievements, and strategic opportunities — a systematic review (PRISMA 2020)
items.samenvatting_bron: Under Vision 2030, Saudi Arabia has rebuilt its environmental governance around the 2020/21 Environment Law, the National Center for Environmental Compliance, the Saudi Green Initiative (SGI), and ISO 14001/EIA alignment. This review sets out that framework, draws together outcomes across biodiversity, air, water, waste, and climate/energy, and flags priority gaps for Vision 2030 and comparable jurisdictions. The search, conducted to PRISMA 2020 standards, covered Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and Google Scholar, supplemented by reference-list and grey-literature screening against a pre-specified PECO frame. All records were screened by the author; a second screener dual-screened a 20% sample. Quality was appraised with JBI checklists, and certainty was rated using a GRADE-informed approach. Of 3,512 records screened after de-duplication, 78 sources met inclusion criteria, spanning six domains: governance and compliance institutions; biodiversity (protected-area coverage grew from ~4% to 18.1% of land); air quality (~240 stations; declining PM2.5, NOx, SO2); water (>200 plants; 100% urban-reuse target); waste (2021 Waste Management Law; 85-90% diversion by 2035-2040); and clean energy/climate (50% renewable electricity by 2030; net-zero by 2060; expanding CCUS/hydrogen). Certainty was moderate for governance, low to moderate for environmental quality (largely government reports), and low for projections. items.titel: Smart water management in agriculture: convergence of sensors, imaging, AI, precision irrigation, and robotics systems
items.samenvatting_bron: Agricultural irrigation systems can bear the heavy losses of water through runoff, evaporation, and deep percolation. Crop water requirements vary with crop species, growth stage, soil properties, evapotranspiration, weather, and plant water status; therefore, irrigation scheduling based on a single parameter is insufficient. Conventional water management systems often rely on uniform application, fixed scheduling, and limited real-time information, which overlooks spatial and temporal variation in soil, crop, and weather conditions and can result in water loss, over-irrigation, and under-irrigation. This review highlights studies on the integration of AI-driven sensing and imaging technologies, IoT-based precision irrigation, variable-rate technologies, digital twins, and agricultural robotics for crop water management. These approaches integrate field, crop, weather, and spatial information to support water-demand assessment, crop-stress monitoring, irrigation scheduling, site-specific application, and automated water management. The reviewed studies report water savings, improved water-use efficiency, crop performance, and more site-specific irrigation and input application across different crops and irrigation systems. The review also highlights the limitations of these systems, including sensing reliability, model transferability, connectivity, interoperability, cybersecurity, investment costs, and environmental effects.
