items.samenvatting_bron: Three marine protected areas, i.e., Borkum Reef Ground, Sylt Outer Reef, and Dogger Bank, have been established within the European NATURA 2000 program in the German Exclusive Economic Zone of the North Sea. Within them, we analysed the effect of the varying impact of mobile bottom-contact fishing on infauna communities in selected focus areas as a baseline study prior to the exclusion of mobile bottom-contact fishing since 2023. The three focus areas varied significantly in sediment composition and depth. The mobile bottom-contact fishing intensity was lowest at Borkum Reef Ground, but revealed decreasing gradients at Sylt Outer Reef and Dogger Bank. The infauna communities in the three focus areas were significantly different. Gradients in sediment composition, e.g. sand, mud, gravel and shell contents, revealed significant relationships with the infauna communities in the three areas. But on a small spatial scale also the gradients of mobile bottom-contact fishing intensity correlated significantly with the variations of the infauna communities at Sylt Outer Reef and Dogger Bank. The common agreement of the European Commission for the exclusion of mobile bottom-contact fishing in parts of Borkum Reef Ground and Sylt Outer Reef since 2023 and of Dogger Bank since 2025 will provide the opportunity to study the recovery of the infauna communities in these areas from mobile bottom-contact fishing in future.

items.titel: Circular Transformation in the Silk Sector: A Fuzzy Delphi–DEMATEL Analysis of Critical Factors
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT The circular transformation in the silk industry is crucial for enhancing resource efficiency and minimizing waste. Despite growing interest in circularity within the textile sector, the silk industry remains underexplored. This study addresses this gap by systematically assessing the barriers and enablers influencing circular economy adoption in silk. A two‐stage methodology was applied. First, a comprehensive literature review combined with expert input identified key factors, which were then validated using the fuzzy Delphi method (FDM) with 16 experts from industry and academia, resulting in nine barriers and 12 enablers. Next, the Decision‐Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) technique examined the prominence and causal relationships among these factors. Results indicate that lack of policy support from fashion brands, ineffective planning, and inadequate communication are the most significant barriers, while limited consumer awareness and high technology costs strongly influence other barriers. Key enablers include upcycling business models, rediscovery of silk knowledge, and waste material recovery. Resource efficiency culture, design for longevity, and traditional expertise act as causal drivers. The study provides actionable guidance for managers, policymakers, and researchers, offering practical and theoretical insights to advance circularity in silk.

items.titel: The Silent Spaces of Cultural Heritage: The Transformation of Archaeological Excavation Houses
items.samenvatting_bron: With the development of the discipline of archaeology, excavation houses emerged initially as temporary shelter solutions; over time, however, the extension of excavation periods, the diversification of working conditions, and the increase in interdisciplinary studies led them to evolve into more permanent and functional spaces. It is observed that excavation houses do not possess a fixed typology; rather, various spatial forms—from tents and school buildings to prefabricated structures, as well as historical and modern buildings—have been utilized for this purpose. Today, excavation houses have become multifunctional environments that not only serve as places of accommodation and work, but also enhance the quality of archaeological practice, support public awareness, and contribute to the transmission of cultural heritage. In this study, the spatial transformation of archaeological excavation houses throughout the historical process has been examined and evaluated through selected case studies. Excavation houses are addressed under two main categories—temporary and permanent accommodation—and, based on research and observations, these categories are further divided into subcategories and analyzed through examples. The fact that excavation houses have not previously been examined within this scope, and that no comparable study has been encountered in the literature, highlights the original contribution of this research.

items.titel: The Mitochondria-Modulating Small Molecule TEM1657 Suppresses NFKBIZ Pathway and Resolves Th17-Driven Psoriatic Inflammation
items.samenvatting_bron: Psoriasis is a chronic skin disease characterized by red, scaly plaques mainly driven by dysregulated T cells that induce keratinocytes (KCs) proliferation and inflammation. Despite significant advancements in disease management through biologics and topical therapies, these treatments offer only temporary relief and fail to prevent disease recurrence. Considering the current therapeutic needs, we described herein a novel small molecule TEM1657, derived from 3,5-dicaffeoylquinic acid with anti-inflammatory potency in imiquimod-induced psoriasis mouse model as well as in Th17-stimulated KCs. These observations highlighted a pathway that represents an innovative target in psoriasis and other NFKBIZ-related disorders.

items.samenvatting_bron: Introduction Wheat powdery mildew poses a serious threat to global wheat production, and its accurate identification is key to smart agriculture. Building on this, the LCRNet model was proposed, which effectively processes fluorescence image data through a collaborative mechanism integrating the Large Selective Adaptive Fusion (LSAF) and Coordinated Attention (CA) modules. Full-panel results show no strong and consistent average relationship between the climate variables and real GDP per capita across estimators. items.titel: Development of Irrigation Automation System Based on FAO Penman-Monteith Model with Drip Irrigation for Paddy Rice
items.samenvatting_bron: The increasing demand on water due to drought impacts paddy rice production. Therefore, the use of sustainable irrigation methods and smart agricultural practices are of gaining importance. In this study, it was aimed to provide drip irrigation automation by calculating paddy rice evapotranspiration (ETC), irrigation water requirement and irrigation duration based on FAO Penman-Monteith (FAO-PM) model with the developed prototype device via mobile application. Four different irrigation levels (S100, S150, S200 and Farmer (F)) were applied in the study. The research was carried out in the farmer's field located in İpsala district of Edirne province in 2023 and 2024 seasons. The trial was carried out based on daily meteorological parameters in field conditions and the data were stored in a Sheets file on Google Drive. In the study, the seasonal total reference evapotranspiration (ET0) and ETC values were calculated as 571 and 583 mm in 2023 and 655 and 665 mm in 2024. Ranges of seasonal total irrigation water applied were 695-1555 mm in 2023 and 802-1916 mm in 2024. In the second year of the study, the highest yield was obtained in the F application at 7401 kg/ha, while the lowest yield was obtained in the S100 application at 5381 kg/ha. items.titel: Verkhnodniprovsk Digital Twin Feasibility Model: Synthetic Scenarios for River Cooling, Heat Pumps and Seasonal Cold Storage
items.samenvatting_bron: Анотація (Description / Abstract) This release presents a digital-twin feasibility model and synthetic simulation dataset for exploratory assessment of climate-adaptation infrastructure in Verkhnodniprovsk, Ukraine. It connects synthetic climate statistics and a conceptual urban master plan with models of green-route irrigation, building cooling, water-source heat-pump heating, and seasonal cold storage. The workflow supports comparison of infrastructure options and operating strategies before subsequent field investigation and pilot implementation. The modelling framework combines a synthetic weather generator with simplified reservoir-temperature, root-zone water-balance, building-load, heat-pump, and cold-storage models. Operational comparisons include fixed and forecast-based irrigation, air and river-assisted cooling, hybrid cooling with air backup, and alternative rules for dispatching stored cold. Seasonal storage combines sensible and latent water–ice capacity with winter charging by passive thermosyphons and simplified representations of insulation losses and groundwater-related heat gains. The reference experiments use 50 synthetic seasons for each of three summer heat scenarios, with 92 days per summer. Winter simulations cover 151 days and warming increments from 0 to 3 K. items.titel: Climate Change and Maternal Health in Urban Nigeria: Heat, Flood Risk, Mental Health, and Health System Adaptation Gaps
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban Nigeria is experiencing increasing exposure to climate-related hazards, including extreme heat, recurrent flooding, and environmental degradation, which pose significant risks to maternal health. Pregnancy represents a physiologically sensitive period, during which elevated temperatures, disrupted access to care, infectious exposures, and psychosocial stress can contribute to adverse maternal, perinatal, and mental health outcomes. This narrative review synthesizes existing literature on the pathways linking climate hazards to maternal health outcomes in urban Nigeria. Heat exposure is associated with dehydration, preterm birth, hypertensive disorders, and stillbirth, whereas flooding contributes to infection risk, malaria exposure, disrupted antenatal care, and nutritional insecurity. Climate-related stressors also affect maternal mental health, manifesting as anxiety, climate grief, economic stress, amplified domestic tension, and increased postpartum depression risk. Urban health system vulnerabilities — including flood-damaged facilities, limited emergency obstetric transport, weak climate adaptation planning, and fragmented surveillance systems — further exacerbate these risks. Policy analysis reveals a disconnect between Nigeria's climate adaptation frameworks and maternal health strategies. items.titel: Spatiotemporal mapping of agricultural drought using geospatial approach in the East Bale Zone, Ethiopia
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Agricultural drought significantly threatens food security, livelihoods, and ecosystem stability, especially in regions prone to drought, such as the East Bale zone. This study investigates the spatial and temporal patterns of agricultural drought over 30 years (1993–2024) by combining meteorological station data with satellite‐derived vegetation and thermal indices. To assess meteorological drought, the standardized precipitation index (SPI) was calculated at 3‐, 6‐, and 12‐month intervals. For agricultural and thermal stress analysis, remote sensing‐based indices including the vegetation condition index (VCI), temperature condition index, and vegetation health index (VHI) were utilized. The results indicate that the years 2003, 2008, and 2018 experienced the most severe droughts, as shown consistently across all indices. Spatial analysis revealed that the central, southern, and eastern lowland areas faced the highest frequency and severity of drought, while the northwestern highlands remained comparatively resilient. Cross‐index correlation revealed strong agreement between SPI and VCI ( R 2 = 0.77), and between VHI and VCI ( R 2 = 0.83), supporting the effectiveness of integrated drought monitoring approaches. This research advances the field of drought assessment by enhancing spatial and temporal resolution and validating cross‐index relationships at the subregional level. items.titel: Digital Agricultural Transformation under Climate Risk: A Policy and Financing Perspective within the National Economy Model
items.samenvatting_bron: Today, the global food system is undergoing a multidimensional transformation driven by climate change, population growth and rising food demand. Irregular precipitation regimes, increasing water scarcity and ecosystem degradation are making agricultural production increasingly unpredictable and fragile. In addition to these ecological pressures, shrinking arable land, the ageing agricultural labour force and rising input costs further challenge the sustainability of conventional farming systems. The growing frequency of extreme weather events demonstrates the vulnerability of existing production models and highlights the need for structural transformation in agriculture. Digital agriculture offers a potential solution through a technology-oriented paradigm shift. Technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI)-based decision support systems, remote sensing and precision agriculture enable site-specific resource management, reducing environmental impact while improving productivity. However, the adoption of these technologies is constrained by high investment costs and financial uncertainty, particularly for small and medium-scale producers. Therefore, integrating digital technologies into agricultural production depends on reducing financial and operational risks through effective public policy instruments. items.titel: Illuminating gendered pathways: Exploring energy service demands in rural and peri-urban Nigeria
items.samenvatting_bron: Gender gaps in energy access are well documented, but evidence on who prioritises which electrical appliances and why remains limited. This paper investigates links between appliance needs, gender roles, and intra-household decision-making in rural and peri-urban Nigeria. Using a mixed-methods design, it combines individual interviews and focus group discussions with a household survey (n = 3599). Qualitatively, appliance priorities are examined together with user values — via the User Perceived Value Game — to understand what appliances mean in everyday life. Quantitatively, appliance ownership is analysed using logistic and conditional logistic regression models, linked to a measure of women’s decision-making within the household. Women and men show substantial overlap in high-priority appliances, with mobile phones, fans, and televisions consistently ranking at the top. At the same time, systematic divergences emerge, with women placing greater emphasis on fridges and blenders, whereas men prioritise radios and torches. Group deliberations mirror these patterns but also reveal how group gender composition can mute gender-specific preferences. Value narratives indicate a largely shared set of values across genders, with device-specific differences partly shaped by gender roles. items.titel: The final count-down: estimating the total value of all the world's natural resources and an estimate of how long they may last
items.samenvatting_bron: Introduction We have attempted a final count-down of all resources available to human society in future and converted this to monetary value for 2026. Methods Simulations using the WORLD7 Integrated Assessment Model explore how long the available resources will support wealth and value creation in the global society. Results The estimates made suggests that about 75% of the world's value creation has its origin in natural resources, and about 2 / 3 of the value creation has its origin in finite, fossil natural resources, fossil energy, fossil metals, and fossil materials. Our results suggests that a system reconfiguration, including thorium-based technologies, would be required for making society last more than 1,000 generations. The most valuable resources in analysis are the energy resources, but these are partly dependent on the availability of technology metals and materials. Thorium appears to be the single most valuable energy resource on the list, provided thorium-based power plants are adopted, and based on the energy price. The recoverable resource stocks of natural resources and the annual extraction rates were estimated. items.titel: Prioritizing climate-resilient housing recovery in conflict-affected Yemen: a district-level MCDA and uncertainty framework
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Yemen’s housing recovery requires choices among districts where flood exposure, conflict, displacement and humanitarian need overlap. This study develops a district-level multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) framework to identify districts that remain high priorities for early climate-resilient housing recovery under alternative assumptions. The model combines seven dimensions: flood hazard, human exposure, built exposure, climate stress, conflict fragility, displacement pressure and humanitarian severity. Four weighting scenarios are tested, and Monte Carlo perturbation examines rank stability when normalized inputs and scenario weights vary. The model does not estimate direct housing damage; it screens districts under combined physical and social pressures and compares the national ranking with heterogeneous city-level evidence. The highest-ranked districts are Ma’rib, Ma’rib City, Sirwah, Al Marawi’ah, Khur Maksar, Ad Durayhimi, Tuban and Bani Sa’d. Flood-gate, missing-data, internal-weight and sparse-RDT ablation tests preserve the leading pattern, although uncertainty increases near selection thresholds. The framework provides a transparent national screening tool for recovery sequencing, subject to local engineering assessment and stakeholder validation before implementation.

items.titel: FRAMEWORK DEVELOPMENT OF BIOPHILIC MODEL FOR CORPORATE BUILDINGS
items.samenvatting_bron: Environmental degradation and unorganized cities are rising issues because of a growing population in an era of fast globalization. People confronted a dilemma with denser and congested urban development, which highlighted the fragility of towns and their residents. There are no such rules that govern the general equilibrium of the ecosystem due to rising urbanization and unplanned cities. As a result, global temperatures will rise by 1.5 degrees Celsius by 2050. Rapid building has made a substantial impact on the natural world to meet the requirements of a rising population. It contributes to global warming by generating more than 30% of the world's emissions of greenhouse gases. Buildings are the largest energy consumers and equivalent to approximately 40% of all substantial energy sources for example nuclear energy, hydropower, and fossil fuels. Sustainable construction and development methods are being used to reduce negative consequences and create an environment that is more environmentally friendly. Applying biophilic design concepts in building construction to generate connections between individuals and the environment is one method of achieving sustainability. The various categories of biophilic design are identified, evaluated, and their key components discussed in this study's thorough literature research. items.titel: When heat hits: Short-run saving and withdrawal behavior among microfinance clients in Benin
items.samenvatting_bron: Increased access to finance is widely viewed as a key driver to increase adaptive capacity in response to climate change. However, apart from limited studies on borrowing behavior, little is known about how exposure to extreme heat is associated with microfinance clients’ financial behavior. This study addresses this gap by investigating the short-run associations of unusual heat with microfinance clients’ saving and withdrawal behavior. In a case study, it combines geo-located temperature data with a unique dataset of around 50,000 clients of a leading Microfinance Institution (MFI) in Benin. Applying two-way fixed effects, seemingly unrelated regression, and ordinary least squares models, the study finds that exposure to extreme heat is heterogeneously associated with microfinance clients’ financial behavior. Specifically, non-agricultural clients show suggestive evidence of the accumulation of precautionary savings after extreme heat days in the preceding quarter, while extreme heat days are negatively associated with agricultural clients’ savings. Microfinance clients increase their withdrawals when exposed to extreme heat within the preceding quarter, but the association is not robust for agricultural clients’ withdrawals in response to an increase in annual extreme heat days. items.titel: Agronomic and Nutritional Perspectives on Vegetable Crops in Africa
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT Vegetable production plays a crucial role in food security, nutrition, and livelihoods across Africa. Yet, it faces persistent challenges related to climate variability, water scarcity, soil degradation, and limited access to agricultural inputs. This review synthesizes current agronomic, nutritional, and socio‐economic perspectives on vegetable production systems in Africa, with a particular emphasis on sustainability and resilience. Key agronomic strategies, including improved irrigation practices, integrated nutrient management, and the use of biostimulants, are discussed as pathways to enhance productivity under resource‐constrained conditions. Agronomic practices are discussed in terms of their influence not only on crop productivity but also on nutritional composition, phytochemical accumulation, postharvest quality, and food safety, whereas the role of indigenous knowledge systems in supporting climate adaptation, soil health, biodiversity conservation, and low‐input farming practices is also considered. From a phytochemical and nutritional standpoint, African indigenous vegetables emerge as underutilized yet highly valuable crops, rich in vitamins, essential elements, and bioactive compounds with antioxidant and anti‐inflammatory properties. These attributes position vegetables not only as sources of nourishment but also as functional foods with the potential to address micronutrient deficiencies and reduce the burden of non‐communicable diseases. items.titel: EXPLORING VERTICAL GREENING SYSTEM FOR ENHANCING THERMAL COMFORT IN THE DESIGN OF POSTGRADUATE HOSTEL FOR GOMBE STATE UNIVERSITY, GOMBE, NIGERIA
items.samenvatting_bron: The concept of vertical greening systems has gained considerable attention in recent years as an innovative approach to enhancing thermal comfort within various built environments. This growing interest is rooted in the recognition of the substantial influence that greenery can exert on the microclimate of structures. The design of student hostels in general faces a significant challenge on thermal discomfort, intensified by high solar gain in the tropical savannah climate. Traditional building materials offer minimal insulation, leading to increased reliance on energy intensive cooling systems. In this regard, the integration of vertical greening systems presents an intriguing opportunity to not only improves the aesthetic appeal of the building but also to create a more comfortable and sustainable living environment for its occupants. By exploring the potential benefits and challenges associated with these systems, this research focuses on investigating the effectiveness of vertical greening systems in improving thermal comfort within the design of a postgraduate student hostel at Gombe State University. The study aims to evaluate the influence of these systems on creating a more comfortable living environment. The study employs a case study approach to analyze selected buildings. items.titel: THE NETWORKING OF AI-DRIVEN IMPROVED SANITATION ARCHITECTURE INNOVATIONS, STRATEGIES AND SOLUTIONS TOWARDS ODF IN BAUCHI BUILT ENVIRONMENT
items.samenvatting_bron: The quest for the pursuit of Open Defecation Free (ODF) status in Nigeria, particularly in states like Bauchi, has historically relied on conventional Community-Led Total Sanitation (CLTS) approaches. However, the sustainability of these interventions is often compromised by inadequate facility maintenance, poor design aesthetics, and lack of economic incentives. This paper explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and improved toilet architecture innovations as a transformative strategy for achieving and sustaining ODF in the Bauchi built environment. By leveraging AI-driven generative design, parametric modeling, and Internet of Things (IoT) predictive maintenance, architects and urban planners can develop culturally resonant, climate-resilient, and economically viable sanitation facilities. This research proposes a framework where AI algorithms analyze local topographical, climatic, and socio-cultural data to generate optimized architectural designs for public and communal toilets. Furthermore, the integration of AI-powered digital twins and smart sensors facilitates real-time monitoring of facility usage, structural integrity, and environmental impact. The findings suggest that AI-driven architectural innovations can significantly enhance community acceptance, reduce slippage from ODF status, and foster sustainable sanitation practices in Bauchi State.

Our results suggest that this technique would detect SO2 injections, at the horizontal and vertical scale, within hours to a few days since the SAI deployment. This concept would quantify the SO2 injected mass, even for injections of the order of magnitude of a few to some tens of tonnes of SO2, characteristic of "near-term" to "mid-term" experiments feasible even unilaterally/illegally, or in the context of small-scale outdoor experiments, with presently existing technology and at relatively low cost. In addition, our results suggest that this concept would be able to track the temporal evolution of the subsequently formed SA, as it spreads zonally and then toward higher latitudes through meridional dispersion, and to monitor changes in its vertical distribution over time through processes like self-lofting of the resulting SA plume. items.titel: Trade‐Offs in Sustainable Development? The Relationship Between the Sustainable Development Goals and Circular Economy Outcomes in the European Union
items.samenvatting_bron: ABSTRACT Countries around the world have committed to a range of sustainable development initiatives aimed at advancing the Sustainable Development Goals and promoting the circular economy. However, the implementation of these sustainability initiatives entails substantial costs and resource requirements which may result in potential trade‐offs. We examine these sustainability trade‐offs by focusing on the relationship between the Sustainable Development Goals and the circular economy. Drawing on a panel dataset of European Union member states spanning 2009–2021, we find that progress on the Sustainable Development Goals is negatively associated with circular economy outcomes, indicating potential trade‐offs between these major sustainability initiatives. Furthermore, we find that strong environmental policy settings within ruling governments, higher levels of government spending, and greater trade freedom positively moderate the relationship between the Sustainable Development Goals and circular economy outcomes, thereby reducing sustainability trade‐offs. The findings of this study contribute to extant theory and have implications for policymakers.

items.titel: Developing a resource-based analysis of technological innovation systems: The case of digital innovation in Dutch processing industries
items.samenvatting_bron: Resource-based perspectives in Technological Innovation Systems (TIS) research offer new insights into innovation dynamics and address gaps in the traditional structure-function approach. We take stock of this perspective to develop a framework that enhances TIS in two ways. First, we improve the conceptual linkage between TIS elements and functions by focusing on innovation resources and their dynamics. Next, we offer a combined view of system-building and hindering processes by identifying and characterizing meso-level TIS mechanisms through micro-level resource changes. We apply our framework to a qualitative case study on the digital TIS within the Dutch processing industry. The analysis generalizes four system-building activities and four systemic problems, which emerge from the presence, accessibility, applicability, and scale of innovation resources. Additionally, four case-specific mechanisms are identified which illustrate tensions between positive and negative dynamics, revealing fundamental complexity underlying the overall TIS functioning. Our framework provides a basis for unpacking such tensions and identifying more targeted policy interventions, particularly for innovation systems of general-purpose technologies.

items.titel: Changes in travel time ratios (TTR) before and during the first COVID-19 lockdown in Austria
items.samenvatting_bron: COVID-19 has profoundly affected travel behaviour, and numerous studies have examined its impact on daily activities. However, relatively little attention has been paid to the trade-offs between activity-location choices, associated travel times, and the durations of activities undertaken at those locations. This paper addresses this gap by analysing how long individuals travel to reach different activity destinations and how much time they ultimately spend there, and how this balance varies across trip purposes, journey structures, and socio-demographic groups before and during the COVID-19 lockdown. The analysis draws on two waves of a seven-day travel and time-use diary survey conducted in Austria. Consistent with previous research, the results confirm that both the number of journeys and the frequency of out-of-home activities declined sharply during the lockdown. However, changes in the trade-off between travel time and activity duration were heterogeneous across activity purposes, journey types, and socio-demographic groups. In particular, work-related activities generally exhibited declining Travel Time Ratio (TTR) values, while several discretionary activities showed increases. These differentiated shifts reflect systematic differences in socio-demographic characteristics, activity structures, and journey configurations, indicating that individuals adjusted unevenly to altered capability, authority, and coupling constraints. items.titel: Culture Wars: Subcreation and the Narrative Contestation of Cultivated Meat
items.samenvatting_bron: Cultivated meat – meat grown from animal cells in bioreactors – has become a symbolic flashpoint in contemporary culture wars, framed not as a technical innovation but as either moral salvation or civilizational threat. We argue that these conflicts arise through temporalized narrative subcreation: the construction of emotionally charged storyworlds that embed cultural values within divergent orientations toward past and future, continuity and change. Analyzing proponent and opponent discourse, we show how both sides mobilize the same core values – tradition, identity, and autonomy – yet transform them into polarized narratives by projecting them into distinct temporal storyworld genres. Our framework theorizes culture wars as contests of temporal meaning-making, where legitimacy hinges on competing subcreated worlds that render innovations morally legible. By revealing the temporal and narrative structures underpinning these conflicts, we offer a portable analytic lens for understanding legitimacy struggles surrounding other disruptive innovations, including climate action, reproductive technologies, and AI governance.

items.titel: Institutional risk, finance, and the limits of techno-economic optimality in green hydrogen deployment
items.samenvatting_bron: Green hydrogen is widely positioned as a key option for deep decarbonization, yet large-scale deployment remains limited despite growing techno-economic potential. This review examines how non-technical conditions influence the feasibility of green hydrogen business models, using the Netherlands as an illustrative case. A review-driven mixed-methods framework integrates evidence from a systematic literature review, semi-structured expert interviews, and an established hourly-resolved techno-economic optimization model to examine how policy design, investment risk, infrastructure constraints, and demand formation influence both the levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) and deployment feasibility. A multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) is employed to synthesize qualitative and quantitative evidence and prioritize the principal drivers and barriers identified across the different sources. The synthesized evidence, supported by the illustrative techno-economic analysis, indicates that LCOH values below €6 kg −1 are attainable under favorable assumptions, including low renewable electricity prices, reduced weighted average cost of capital (WACC), and access to underground hydrogen storage. However, regulatory fragmentation, grid congestion, weak demand coordination, and limited institutional legitimacy substantially constrain the realization of such conditions in practice. items.titel: The four ways of knowing: revising the 4P model of knowing through a non-dual and reflexive perspective
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Vervaeke and Mastropietro’s 4P model of knowing is a non-representational and process-oriented framework that integrates four interrelated ways of knowing: propositional, procedural, perspectival, and participatory. In this paper, we revise this model, drawing on the enactive approach and insights from Madhyamaka and Yogācāra Buddhist traditions of philosophy. We first provide an integrated overview of the 4P model and identify three questions concerning the conceptualization of participatory knowing and the ontological status of distinctions between the four ways of knowing. We then introduce the enactive and Buddhist resources that inform our treatment, and address these questions through a non-dual and reflexive treatment that preserves the framework’s pedagogical and transformative potential. Finally, we discuss how the revised framework can inform fields as diverse as education, psychotherapy, and contemplative pedagogy.

items.titel: Double energy vulnerability in Eastern Europe: quantifying and verifying regional sensitivity to the phenomenon
items.samenvatting_bron: This study considers 57 regions from 8 Eastern European countries and quantifies the sensitivity to double energy vulnerability of each region by developing a composite indicator. Double energy vulnerability is a concept describing simultaneous exposure to energy and transport poverty. Eastern European countries present high levels of double energy vulnerability; nonetheless, remaining an understudied macro-region. To understand the dependency between double energy vulnerability and rurality and tenure, the results are then compared with the rurality levels of the different regions, and to the national proportion spent on energy and transport services. The developed indicator provides an analysis of the phenomenon across Eastern Europe, quantifying regions' sensitivity to it by combining indicators stemming from different dimensions. Data from 2015 to 2024 was considered. Bulgaria is found to be the country presenting the highest level of double energy vulnerability. For the latter specifically, data at higher spatial resolution was utilised to have a more detailed understanding and to assess the obtained results. Finally, the results were verified by performing interviews with relevant experts in the field, considering also non-quantifiable aspects. The results provide a clearer picture of Eastern European regions' sensitivity to double energy vulnerability, highlighting the most sensitive ones.

items.titel: Interdisciplinary Research on Real Estate
items.samenvatting_bron: The proceedings of the Conference of Interdisciplinary Research on Real Estate (CIRRE) from 2016–2025 demonstrate the evolution of real estate research into an interdisciplinary, human-centred, and systems-oriented field that addresses complex societal, environmental, and technological challenges. A key lesson is the importance of integrating perspectives from law, economics, architecture, engineering, sociology, psychology, and environmental sciences. This interdisciplinary approach enables more comprehensive solutions to issues such as housing inequality, urban resilience, and sustainable development. Human well-being has remained a central focus throughout the decade. Research increasingly emphasizes residential satisfaction, participatory planning, accessibility, and the needs of aging populations, culminating in studies on aging in place and smart home technologies. This reinforces the principle that successful real estate solutions should prioritize users’ quality of life alongside technical and economic objectives. Sustainability has evolved from a conceptual aspiration into a practical imperative. CIRRE research highlights low-carbon development, circular economy principles, energy-efficient renovations, and resilience to climate change and global crises, emphasizing the integration of environmental, social, and economic sustainability. items.titel: Switching Patterns of Oral Retinoids to Alternative Medications: An Interrupted Time-Series Analysis of Four European Countries
items.samenvatting_bron: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: The European Pregnancy Prevention Program for oral retinoids was updated in 2018, yet its impact on switching to retinoid alternative medications remains unclear. The utilisation of retinoid alternative medications and switching from oral retinoids to retinoid alternative medications after discontinuation were measured. Changes in the rates of switching before and after implementation of the Pregnancy Prevention Program were analysed using an interrupted time series analysis. RESULTS: From 88,992 women of childbearing potential previously exposed to retinoids, 32.0% (28,446) switched to a retinoid alternative medication over the study period. Overall, ten out of 80 median discontinuers per month switched. Median switching monthly rates ranged from 1.8 to 6.5% and from 1.2 to 2.3% pre-implementation and post-implementation, respectively. items.titel: REScoops acting as intermediaries, influencing the scaling of energy communities; a multi-case analysis of five pilots in Europe
items.samenvatting_bron: There is increasing scholarly attention to the scaling of energy communities (EC). Intermediaries have an important role here. Energy communities themselves, especially in the form of renewable energy cooperatives (REScoops), can take on this role very well. This paper addresses the question how REScoops, acting as intermediaries, influence the scaling of ECs. A longitudinal multi-case research design is adopted to answer this question. Five cases of EC pilots in different EU countries receiving intermediary support from REScoops were selected and researched over a three-year period. Data collection involved interviews, text documents, a quantitative longitudinal survey, and pilot project data. Results show that EC organisations use various forms of scaling: scaling-up, -out, and -deep. Regarding REScoops acting as an intermediary influencing the scaling of ECs, the analysis presents moderate support for positive impact. The relationship appears positive for scaling-deep and fairly positive for scaling-out. For scaling-up the relationship there was mostly within-case evidence. Scaling-up appears related to contextual factors. A fairly challenging context seems correlated to ECs deploying scaling-up strategies, using REScoop intermediary agency with the aim of changing key institutional structures, regulatory and policy frameworks that have a negative impact on ECs. This paper ends with suggestions for future work.

items.titel: Bony labyrinth taxonomic identification and long-term evolution of livestock in the Southwest and Central Asia
items.samenvatting_bron: Southwest and Central Asia were pivotal regions for the domestication and dispersal of domestic herbivores. Here we investigate long-term variation in bony labyrinth morphology of domestic bovids (sheep, goats and cattle) across the last 10 000 years. We focused on the osseous cavity of the inner ear, located within the petrous bone. We analysed semicircular canal (SC) size and shape using micro-computed tomography and geometric morphometrics (GMM) on 78 modern reference specimens and 234 archaeological petrous bones from 51 sites spanning the Iranian Plateau, Central Asia, the Caucasus and the Indus Valley. Bony labyrinth morphometrics yielded a strong taxonomic signal, enabling species-level identification of 228 out of 234 specimens and revealing greater diversity than anticipated. Comparative analyses further documented contrasting, nonlinear diachronic trajectories in SC size and shape among sheep, goats and cattle, reflecting species-specific responses to domestication and long-term herd management. Together, these results demonstrate that bony labyrinth GMM provides a robust, non-destructive framework for taxonomic identification and evolutionary inference and underscore how long-term, interdisciplinary approaches can capture the complex, nonlinear dynamics of animal domestication across the longue durée.

items.titel: Poisoned arrows in the Danish Early Mesolithic: Testing lithic ballistic morphometrics against faunal and archaeobotanical data
items.samenvatting_bron: Throughout human deep history, lithic tool components became periodically very small. Such microlithic tools are the signature artefacts of the European Mesolithic in general, and the iconic Danish Mesolithic in particular. Sandwiched between the end of the Pleistocene and the emergence of agricultural lifeways, the Danish Mesolithic is characterised by marked changes in microlith design from lanceolates to geometrics and finally to transversal forms with wide front edges. These changes are synonymous with the transitions between the traditionally defined cultures of the Early, Middle and Late Mesolithic, yet the forces shaping them remain opaque. Here we present lithic, faunal, and a combination of archaeobotanical and palaeobotanical proxies, suggesting that the use of arrow poison was a likely driver for microlithic design change. An analysis of ballistically relevant morphometric attributes of lithics found in direct association with hunted prey suggests that the use of poison was prevalent during the Early Mesolithic when targeted game animals were also largest. Thereafter, lithic projectile points became larger and game animals smaller, likely reflecting Holocene faunal downsizing alongside changing hunting strategies. Palaeobotanical evidence from Denmark and southern Sweden suggests that a wide range of toxic plants were available throughout the Holocene. items.titel: A Call for Systematic Integration of Family‐Focused Care in Clinical Nursing Practice in Europe: A Position Paper
items.samenvatting_bron: AIM: To highlight the need for a shift to family-focused care and to outline how this transition should be developed and implemented through close collaboration between clinical practice and research. DESIGN: Position paper. METHOD: Members of Family Health in Europe-Research in Nursing (FAME-RN) developed the position paper through an iterative process informed by selected literature, established care models and collective expertise in family nursing. The paper examines distinctions between patient-centred, person-centred, family-centred and family-focused care and considers key barriers, enablers and priorities for implementation across European healthcare settings. RESULTS: Family-focused care recognises families as essential partners in caring for individuals with severe or chronic conditions across the lifespan, working with families as interconnected systems and as an explicit unit of nursing assessment and intervention rather than solely involving them as individuals in care. The position paper identifies key priorities for implementation including conceptual clarity, systematic family assessment, family-level interventions, education and competence development, organisational leadership, supportive policy, co-design with families and implementation-focused research. CONCLUSION: Ensuring that families have access to appropriate information, support and resources enhances caregiving capacity while protecting family health and well-being. items.titel: Strategising social innovation paradoxes: four faces of energy citizenship
items.samenvatting_bron: Social innovation (SI) is an increasingly prominent area of innovation. Involving changes in social relations, SI practice is pervaded with tensions and apparent paradoxes, however. The ‘productive use of paradox’ has been articulated theoretically and demonstrated empirically, but much remains to be elaborated in terms of SI strategies. This contribution explores the SI paradoxes from a paradox management angle. Striving for conceptual insight with empirical concreteness, the analysis invokes the example of energy citizenship. Defined as a shift from passive consumerism towards active political engagement with energy systems, it harbours several tensions. Building on empirical investigations in Belgium, we discuss and strategise four contrasting manifestations of energy citizenship. This empirical diversity helps to showcase paradoxes pertaining to citizenship, intermediation, institutionalisation and materiality. The analysis combines insights from social innovation scholarship, critical innovation studies and governance research to situate these paradoxes in wider SI discussions. Comparing paradox-handling strategies within and across energy citizenship examples, we unpack and nuance the idea of paradoxes as the ‘working substance’ of social innovation. items.titel: Opnieuw eenrichtingsverkeer voor scheepvaart op IJssel door lage waterstand
items.samenvatting_bron: De scheepvaart op de IJssel tussen de IJsselkop en Zutphen mag sinds vanochtend opnieuw maar in één richting varen. Rijkswaterstaat heeft de maatregel opnieuw ingesteld vanwege de lage waterstand. Schepen moeten daardoor weer zo'n 300 kilometer omvaren. Maandag werd het eenrichtingsverkeer nog opgeheven , omdat de minimaal gepeilde diepte op de Boven-IJssel de vereiste 1,45 meter had bereikt. Doordat er minder regen is gevallen dan verwacht, is de waterstand weer onder die grens gedaald, meldt Rijkswaterstaat. De binnenvaart mag nu alleen stroomopwaarts varen. Schepen die vanuit Duitsland de IJssel op willen, kunnen daardoor niet bij Arnhem richting Zutphen varen. Ze moeten omvaren via Amsterdam en het IJsselmeer. Het eenrichtingsverkeer heeft ook gevolgen voor de binnenvaart richting het Twentekanaal, schrijft RTV Oost . Schippers kunnen niet meer vanuit beide richtingen rechtstreeks naar het kanaal varen en moeten dus omvaren. Waterstand blijft dalen Rijkswaterstaat verwacht dat de waterstand de komende vijf dagen verder daalt. Dat hangt onder meer af van de hoeveelheid water die via de Rijn bij Lobith Nederland binnenkomt. Regen in Duitsland en Zwitserland kan ervoor zorgen dat de waterstanden weer stijgen. De waterstanden worden daarom nauwlettend in de gaten gehouden. Als die veranderen, kunnen ook de maatregelen voor de scheepvaart worden aangepast.
